quests.instruction: The shopkeeper says, “We have your size in stock.” If every pair of those football boots had been bought that morning, she would say they were…
quests.hint: What do shelves look like when there’s nothing left to buy?
quests.explanation: In stock means the shop has the item ready. Sold out means all of them have been bought.
quests.funFact: Shops order more of an item when the stock runs low.

quests.instruction: Rina saw a jacket in the window for ₹1,000, the full price. A sign said “20% off today”. Paying less than the normal price is called getting a…
quests.hint: A sign says “20% off today”. What would you get at the till?
quests.explanation: Full price is what something normally costs. A discount takes some of that cost away.
quests.funFact: Many shops hold sales at the end of a season to make room for new stock.

quests.instruction: A sign on the café door says “Please pull”. The sign on the other door, which swings the other way, says, “Please…”
quests.hint: Think of a door you wouldn’t tug toward yourself.
quests.explanation: Pulling brings a door toward you; pushing sends it away. Signs tell you which one each door needs.
quests.funFact: Many doors have flat plates on the push side and handles on the pull side.

quests.instruction: In December, hotels by the beach are full and expensive: the high season. In the rainy months, rooms are cheap and mostly empty: the…
quests.hint: When do hotels offer the best prices?
quests.explanation: High season is the busiest time for travel. Low season is the quietest, with fewer visitors and lower prices.
quests.funFact: Many tourist towns look completely different in the low season, with fewer people and quiet beaches.

quests.instruction: The red hand on the pedestrian signal tells you to wait. When the green walking figure lights up, it’s safe to…
quests.hint: The signal changes and the traffic stops.
quests.explanation: Waiting means staying where you are. Crossing means going over the road when it’s safe.
quests.funFact: Zebra crossings are named for their black-and-white stripes, which look like a zebra’s.

quests.instruction: The bus driver says, “Please sit down while the bus is moving.” Passengers who ignore her and ___ in the aisle could fall over.
quests.hint: Imagine a bus with no empty seats.
quests.explanation: Sitting means resting on a seat. Standing means staying on your feet, which is risky when a bus turns.
quests.funFact: Standing passengers hold on to straps or rails for balance.

quests.instruction: Mum says never to eat wild berries unless an adult confirms they’re safe. Berries that are safe to eat are edible. Some wild berries are…
quests.hint: Why shouldn’t you taste a berry you can’t identify?
quests.explanation: Edible means safe to eat. Poisonous means it can make you ill, so it’s best to leave unknown plants alone.
quests.funFact: Some bright-colored berries and mushrooms are poisonous, so never taste wild plants without an adult.

quests.instruction: A sign in the canteen says, “Take only what you can finish. Please don’t ___ food.”
quests.hint: Take only what you can finish, or the rest goes in the bin.
quests.explanation: To save is to use things carefully. To waste is to throw them away without using them.
quests.funFact: About a third of the food made in the world is lost or wasted.

quests.instruction: The recipe says: “Fill the pot with water, boil the pasta, then ___ the water.”
quests.hint: Before the pasta is served, the water has to go.
quests.explanation: Filling puts liquid in; draining lets it out.
quests.funFact: A colander has holes so the water can drain away while the food stays in.

quests.instruction: The cricket team plays its first match on its own ground: a home match. The next one, in another city, is an…
quests.hint: Whose stadium are they visiting?
quests.explanation: A home match is played on your own ground. An away match is played on the other team’s.
quests.funFact: Teams often get extra support from fans at their home matches.

quests.instruction: The striker kicked the ball past the keeper and into the net: he scored. If it had sailed over the bar, he would have…
quests.hint: Picture a shot flying over the bar.
quests.explanation: To score is to put the ball in the goal. To miss is to fail to.
quests.funFact: In football, the whole ball must cross the line for a goal to count.

quests.instruction: Before the race, the coach has the team jog lightly and stretch to warm up. After the race, they walk slowly to…
quests.hint: After a hard race, a slow walk helps.
quests.explanation: Warming up gets the body ready for hard exercise. Cooling down helps it settle afterward.
quests.funFact: Warming up gets blood flowing to your muscles.

quests.instruction: In Grandmother’s old house, the box of Diwali lights is stored under the roof, in the attic. The jars of pickles are kept below the ground floor in the…
quests.hint: Which part of a house is highest, and which is lowest?
quests.explanation: The attic is the space under the roof. The basement is the space below the ground floor.
quests.funFact: Basements often stay cooler than the rest of the house, which is handy for storing food.

quests.instruction: The baby wakes up at dawn every day. At night, Mum sings softly until she…
quests.hint: Think of what a lullaby is trying to achieve.
quests.explanation: Waking up is going from sleep to being awake. Falling asleep is the reverse.
quests.funFact: Many lullabies have gentle rhythms that help babies relax.

quests.instruction: The class timetable says: Maths starts at 9:00 and ___ at 9:45.
quests.hint: Think of the end of a lesson.
quests.explanation: To start is to begin something. To finish is to bring it to an end.
quests.funFact: Many Indian schools begin the day with an assembly.

quests.instruction: The weather report says the temperature will rise to 38°C at noon, then ___ to 28°C by midnight.
quests.hint: Which way does the temperature move after the hottest part of the day?
quests.explanation: Temperatures rise as the sun climbs and fall as it sets.
quests.funFact: The warmest part of the day is usually in the afternoon, not exactly at noon.

quests.instruction: As monsoon clouds build up, the chances of rain increase. When the clouds pass, the chances…
quests.hint: Think of how the odds of rain change after the clouds go.
quests.explanation: Increasing means getting greater and decreasing means getting smaller.
quests.funFact: Weather apps show the chance of rain as a percentage.

quests.instruction: Sunscreen helps prevent sunburn. Staying in strong sun for hours with no protection is likely to…
quests.hint: Picture bare skin under strong sun for hours.
quests.explanation: To prevent is to stop something from happening. To cause is to make it happen.
quests.funFact: Sunburn is damage to the skin from ultraviolet light.

quests.instruction: While Zoya was online, she chatted with her cousin abroad. When the internet went down, she was…
quests.hint: What do we call a device that isn’t connected to the internet?
quests.explanation: Online means connected to the internet. Offline means not connected.
quests.funFact: The first public website went online in 1991.

quests.instruction: Tara told her grandmother the news over the phone, a spoken message. She also posted a letter, a ___ one.
quests.hint: Think of ink and paper.
quests.explanation: Spoken words are said aloud. Written words are put down on paper or a screen.
quests.funFact: Languages were spoken for thousands of years before anyone wrote them down.

quests.instruction: On a tablet, you can tap a button to hide the menu. Tapping it again will…
quests.hint: Tap the button a second time.
quests.explanation: To hide is to put out of sight. To show is to bring it back into view.
quests.funFact: Most apps use small icons so that menus take up less space.

quests.instruction: The playground rule says every child who wants to join must be welcomed. Telling someone, “You can’t play,” would…
quests.hint: Which action leaves a child out?
quests.explanation: To include is to welcome someone in. To exclude is to leave them out.
quests.funFact: Some playgrounds have equipment designed for children of all abilities to enjoy together.

quests.instruction: A sign near the class art table says: “Please ___ the paints. There’s only one set for the whole group.”
quests.hint: One set of paints, many artists.
quests.explanation: To share is to let others have a turn. To keep is to hold on to something for yourself.
quests.funFact: Paints were once made by grinding minerals and plants into powder.

quests.instruction: Mrs. Iyer reminds the class, “Write down your homework so you don’t ___ it.”
quests.hint: Notes are a safety net for your memory.
quests.explanation: To remember is to keep something in your mind. To forget is to let it slip away.
quests.funFact: Writing things down helps your memory.

quests.instruction: The city plans to build a new park on the empty plot. It would be a pity to ___ the old banyan tree standing there.
quests.hint: What should the builders not do to the tree?
quests.explanation: To build is to make something. To destroy is to wreck it.
quests.funFact: Banyan trees can grow new trunks from roots that hang down from their branches.

quests.instruction: In the morning, mist appears over the pond. As the sun warms the air, it seems to…
quests.hint: Fog doesn’t like heat.
quests.explanation: To appear is to come into view. To disappear is to vanish.
quests.funFact: Fog often forms on cool mornings and clears as the sun warms the air.

quests.instruction: Aunt Leela invites the family to dinner. If everyone’s already busy that night, they can politely ___ the invitation.
quests.hint: There’s a polite way to say no.
quests.explanation: To accept is to say yes. To decline is to politely say no.
quests.funFact: RSVP stands for a French phrase meaning “please reply”.

quests.instruction: The sign at the hill trail says: “It takes two hours to climb to the viewpoint and one hour to…”
quests.hint: Which way is quicker for most people, up or down?
quests.explanation: Climbing goes up; descending goes down.
quests.funFact: Going down a hill is usually faster than going up it.

quests.instruction: If you see a stray dog that looks scared, don’t approach it. Calmly ___ it and tell an adult.
quests.hint: Think of what keeps you at a safe distance.
quests.explanation: To approach is to go closer. To avoid is to keep away from something.
quests.funFact: Many animals bite when they’re frightened, so it’s best to keep a safe distance.

quests.instruction: A sign at the neighborhood book swap says: “Take a book,___ a book.”
quests.hint: A swap works because people do both.
quests.explanation: To take is to receive something. To give is to hand something over. A swap works because people do both.
quests.funFact: Book swaps and little free libraries can be found in neighborhoods around the world.
